name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.24.0 (released 2026-06-04, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.24.0) is the latest release, introducing an opt-in in-memory ACL cache (`auth-access-cache`) to reduce database read load on topic authorization queries, and fixing a critical case-insensitive ACL topic matching security bug on SQLite (PostgreSQL was unaffected). Recent prior releases (v2.20.0–v2.23.0) added S3-compatible object storage for attachments, verified email recipients (`smtp-sender-verify`), per-visitor topic creation rate limits, and several security fixes including SSRF and same-origin script execution vulnerabilities. The project is actively maintained with frequent releases addressing both self-hosting scalability and security hardening.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) / GPL 2.0 (client); dual-licensed — check repository for details
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026 with regular bug fixes and features
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — ACL-based access control with SQLite/PostgreSQL backend, access tokens, and an optional in-memory ACL cache as of v2.24.0
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud version

breaking_excerpts: v2.20.0: ntfy will take full control over the attachment directory or S3 bucket — files matching the message ID format with no database entries will be deleted. Do not reuse the attachment-cache-dir for other purposes.

v2.21.0: smtp-sender-verify flag introduced requiring email address verification before sending notifications; ntfy.sh's AWS SES account was suspended due to unsolicited emails, making verification mandatory on the hosted instance.

v2.24.0: Fix case-insensitive ACL topic matching on SQLite — a rule for 'secret' no longer matches requests for 'SECRET'; existing deployments relying on case-insensitive topic matching will see behavior change.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a versatile open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but it is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server, requiring more integration effort than ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notification mirroring and file sharing but is a proprietary cloud service with a limited free tier and no self-hosting option, unlike ntfy.

alternatives.name: Ntopng Alerts / Alertmanager
alternatives.review: Alertmanager is purpose-built for routing infrastructure alerts from Prometheus and offers rich grouping and silencing rules, but it is not a general-purpose pub-sub notification service like ntfy.
